errors.english: because of which sentient beings are reborn in hells
errors.why: sems can dmyal ba is the word for the hells; the confessant says that by these obscurations he himself would go to the hells, not that sentient beings are reborn there.

fix.find: because of which sentient beings are reborn in hells
fix.replace: because of which I would go to the hells

errors.english: Homage to the Lotus who clearly understands through the playful manifestation of the Tathagata light rays.
errors.why: The name is the Tathāgata Padmajyotirvikrīḍitābhijña: the Tathāgata who knows through the play of lotus light rays; 'Tathāgata' and 'lotus' are swapped.

fix.find: Homage to the Lotus who clearly understands through the playful manifestation of the Tathagata light rays.
fix.replace: Homage to the Tathagata who clearly understands through the playful manifestation of lotus light rays.

errors.english: King of the Victory Banner of Indomitable Power
errors.why: dbang po here is Indra (Indraketudhvajarāja, as the note itself says), not 'indomitable power'.

note: A faithful confession litany overall, but one Buddha name is garbled and the final clause turns the confessant's own rebirth in hell into 'sentient beings' being reborn there.
Accurate rendering of the commentary on the ālambana of atoms, including the Buddhadeva doctrine and the two components of the object-condition.

errors.english: For the followers of the (Samkhya) the Enumerators, an ancient Indian school of dualistic philosophy, the result is clarity
errors.why: ser skya completes drang srong from the previous side: the sage Kapila (for whom the purusha yields serenity), not the Sāṃkhya school (grangs can).

fix.find: For the followers of the (Samkhya) the Enumerators, an ancient Indian school of dualistic philosophy, the result is clarity
fix.replace: For the sage Kapila, the result is clarity

errors.english: By stating "if it is accepted,"
errors.why: The cited phrase is 'even if it is not accepted' (khas mi len na yang).

fix.replace: By stating "even if it is not accepted,"

errors.english: the fundamental reason that the qualities follow after [note: referring to the logical concomitance between the soul and its experiences]
errors.why: The root reason is the objects' being accompanied by (consisting of) the guṇas; the note's 'concomitance between the soul and its experiences' misdescribes it.

note: The argument about the purusha's inferability is followed well, but Kapila is turned into the Sāṃkhya school and a negated root-text lemma is cited as positive.

errors.english: "Come here, I am welcome."
errors.why: The greeting is addressed to the visitor: 'Come, welcome (you have come well)'.

note: Sound rendering of the forest-dweller duties and the start of the miscellaneous duṣkṛta rules, with one garbled greeting.

errors.english: Initially, one should meditate intensely on those who are moderately dear, such as parents and so on.
errors.why: One meditates on the moderately dear AS one's parents etc. (same pattern as the following steps), not on the moderately dear 'such as parents'.

fix.find: Initially, one should meditate intensely on those who are moderately dear, such as parents and so on.
fix.replace: Initially, one should meditate on those who are moderately dear as being like one's parents and so on.

note: Clear and accurate on the three kinds of love and the graded meditation, except that the first step misreads 'as one's parents'.

errors.english: how could one otherwise perceive "this is not similar"?
errors.why: The verse asks how one understands 'this is similar'; there is no negation.

errors.english: If you ask why this occurs through the assembly of causes and conditions without relying on investigation and analysis, we reply:
errors.why: The opponent asserts that the collection of factors comes about by force of causes and is not subject to the challenge 'why is this thus?'; it is a claim, not a question.

note: The upamāna-into-anumāna argument is followed correctly, but a negation is inserted into the staff-bearer verse and the opening objection is recast as a question.

errors.english: the result of grasping the word with certainty is nothing at all
errors.why: sgra nges par gzung ba is the restrictive particle ('only', avadhāraṇa): the word 'only' would have no purpose.

fix.find: the result of grasping the word with certainty is nothing at all
fix.replace: the restrictive word "only" would serve no purpose at all

errors.english: regarding it, you say:
errors.why: bshad pa introduces the author's reply, not the opponent's statement.

errors.english: Because the nature of an action itself cannot follow
errors.why: bya nyid completes gzhal from the previous side: knowability (prameyatva), the kevalānvayin reason under discussion, not 'the nature of an action'.

errors.english: Here, the Logicians have nothing to say because
errors.why: The sentence reports the Naiyāyika's stated position (exclusion from the non-existent is impossible) and then says that point recurs; it does not say the Logicians have nothing to say.

errors.english: [note: original: "vapakṣa"]
errors.why: The term is vipakṣa (and the earlier note's 'anuvaya' should be anvaya).

note: The kevalānvayin debate is broadly tracked, but the reason under discussion is misidentified, the restrictive particle is mistranslated and the author's reply is given to the opponent.

errors.english: The perfect one line of text follows, cut off at the page break
errors.why: Only rdzogs pa'i ('the perfect …') is on the side; the rest is meta-text not in the Tibetan.

fix.find: The perfect one line of text follows, cut off at the page break

note: A faithful verse rendering of the non-conceptual samādhi verses, marred only by stray meta-text at the end.

errors.english: because the student would have already been established previously
errors.why: rje bo is the master/owner, not a student.

fix.find: because the student would have already been established previously
fix.replace: because the master would have already been established previously

errors.english: The remainder is logically untenable.
errors.why: lhag ma is the Nyāya śeṣavat inference ('from the remainder'), a technical term; rendered as plain 'the remainder' here and later ('the remainder is realized later', where the Tibetan says even one who does not know the relation understands the śeṣavat).

note: Sound rendering of the argument about the owner–wealth relation and avinābhāva, with one wrong referent and an unrecognised technical term.

errors.english: yet one possesses that specific perception [note: a mistaken identity of the owner]
errors.why: de'i 'du shes is the perception of it as such (owned by a human), not a mistaken identity; the passage on the absent branch, commissioning and the five māṣakas is run together into one conditional the Tibetan does not have.

errors.english: this specific branch of the primary ritual
errors.why: cho ga in this Vinaya analysis is the procedure/manner of the act (of the fundamental offence), not a ritual.

note: The sthūlātyaya and duṣkṛta cases of mistaken ownership are rendered correctly, but the middle passage on the absent branch and the five māṣakas is muddled.
